event.summary: Old-terminal startup budget excludes socket connect and file cleanup
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: the initial suspicion was that an unresponsive tmux server could make Update wait past the cleanup budget. Checks: Cargo.lock pins tokio 1.53.2 and mio 1.2.4. Their locally installed source shows UnixStream::connect_addr makes a nonblocking connect, propagates EAGAIN rather than retrying, then awaits writable readiness and checks SO_ERROR; it never waits for application accept or a tmux reply. hosts/process.rs:206-210 documents the supported backlog-full outcomes: EAGAIN on Linux, refusal on macOS. end_server handles either as an immediate logged error. Thus a wedged application does not establish the proposed hanging-connect route. remove_server_files (old_terminals.rs:426-450) is outside timeout_at and scans the state directory, so a stalled filesystem or unusually large directory could exceed the stated 15 seconds, but no particular shipped workload or new blocking route was established beyond ordinary asynchronous filesystem calls. Contract: SPEC_impl.md:3000-3003 says the step's own work has one 15-second budget. Suggested bucket: other if a material budget violation route is established. could-be-highest: no security or loss-of-work consequence established or suspected from this lead. Confidence: source-confirmed refutation of the application-unresponsive route; remaining filesystem timing is unverified. proposed_drop: no substantive defect established after checking pinned socket dependencies and cleanup source; not specification acceptance. possible_cover: none. No behavior was observed by execution, and no reproduction was written. Reopen if supported-kernel socket semantics show pending connect without readiness, or a normal shipped state-directory workload demonstrably exceeds the budget.

event.summary: Old-terminal file cleanup runs outside its startup deadline
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4; unchanged cleanup verified at pinned tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db. TLDR: Farhelm's old-terminal cleanup does not enforce its promised startup budget for filesystem cleanup, so this phase can hold a host's return after Update beyond that budget. Details: end_server receives one deadline, but calls remove_server_files directly at lines 182, 244 and 250. That helper at 423-449 awaits read_dir, iterates until end with no entry/time limit, collects matching temporary names, then awaits every unlink; none is inside timeout_at. The elapsed time is recorded only after end_server returns and subtracted from the later sweep's budget, so that accounting cannot cap the cleanup that already ran. Exact contract, SPEC_impl.md:3000-3002: 'the step's own work, the server's end and the sweeps (not the reload's host discovery between them), has one 15-second budget (`OLD_TERMINALS_DEADLINE`), half the 30 seconds the helm allows a supervisor it restarted during Update to come back'. This enforcement gap is source-confirmed; no particular count, healthy-directory delay or measured timeout is claimed. Healthy normal writes are temporary and ordinarily cleaned: files.rs:147-166 says staging cleanup can be skipped by a hard crash, names use fresh UUIDs, and a backstop sweep handles debris; the root otherwise stores fixed metadata plus subdirectories for per-session state. Therefore ordinary session count must not be presented as an unbounded root-file workload. The helper itself imposes no cardinality bound on directory entries or retained crash/failed-cleanup debris, and no bound on asynchronous filesystem completion. No source-backed healthy numeric shape/time bound has been established. The claim is the missing enforcement of an explicit budget, not proof that a typical healthy directory exceeds it. Socket part of original lead is refuted: pinned Cargo.lock has tokio 1.53.2 and mio 1.2.4; tokio src/net/unix/stream.rs:116-128 calls mio connect, waits for writable readiness, then checks SO_ERROR without an application reply. mio src/sys/unix/uds/stream.rs:8-20 accepts only immediate success/EINPROGRESS and returns other errors (including EAGAIN); src/sys/unix/net.rs:15-35 uses SOCK_NONBLOCK on Linux and :58-89 sets O_NONBLOCK with fcntl on macOS. hosts/process.rs:206-210 and SPEC_impl.md:2970-2971 document full-backlog EAGAIN/Linux and refusal/macOS, both promptly logged by end_server. Thus a wedged tmux application alone does not show a hanging-connect route. Suggested bucket: other (deadline contract/enforcement), with high impact requiring an established supported situation causing material Update delay; could-be-highest: no established or suspected security/loss-of-work route from this issue. Confidence: confirmed source-level deadline gap; runtime occurrence and frequency unverified, no execution or reproduction. proposed_drop: false; replaces prior proposed drop because absence of a measured workload does not answer enforcement of the finite declared budget. possible_cover: none known. A remedy would put the entire cleanup await under the existing deadline and log/retain any uncompleted debris for a later start; physical completion of a filesystem syscall may still outlive cancellation, but startup need not wait for it.

event.summary: Failed old-terminal termination still permits Restart
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: after a failure to end an old agent, Farhelm treats it as interrupted and Restart can start another beside it. Details: end_server logs termination failures and sweep times out without preventing conversion; module lines 61-76 describe this deliberately. Suggested bucket: high for duplicate active agents; could-be-highest: potentially, if concurrent agents overwrite user-owned work, but that route is not established here. Confidence: confirmed source behavior, no execution. proposed_drop: explicit specification acceptance, requiring independent check. Exact SPEC.md, Terminal experience, lines 3014-3016: 'A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running.' SPEC_impl.md lines 2999-3001 likewise explicitly accepts startup continuation and duplicate agents. This candidate preserves the original possible consequence; it is not lowered because it is rare. possible_cover: none.

event.summary: Old tab daemons can survive when their tab id is undiscoverable
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: detached work from an old shell tab can remain running after the upgrade until its session is deleted. Details: sweep builds its session set only from converted live old-agent rows and tab-marked snapshot panes; old_tabs obtains other ids from those sessions' scope names, and preserves scopes with terminal-host tab records (launch.rs:890-906 establishes that those records survive until a host is confirmed ended). The set deliberately omits an already-ended old agent's session when its old server cannot be read, and unscoped old tabs then have no recoverable tab id. Suggested bucket: high if unwanted old processes materially persist; could-be-highest: potentially if such work later overwrites user files, but no such consequence route is established in this review. Confidence: confirmed source behavior, no execution. proposed_drop: exact specification acceptance, requiring independent check. SPEC_impl.md:2989-2994 says: 'A whole session is never swept, since its host terminals carry the same session marker; what cannot be attributed to an old tab is left for the session’s Delete, which sweeps the whole session. Once the server is gone, an old tab is found only through the scope units of a session whose agent this start converted, so a scoped tab of any other session (its agent already ended, or in a terminal host), an unscoped tab, and one whose shell’s environment macOS hides wait for that Delete.' SPEC.md:3011-3013 states the same product limitation. possible_cover: none. The original possible user-work consequence is preserved, not lowered because of rarity.
